**Routes and fallback (H-R11 to H-R15, H-R18, H-R19, H-R24)**: `routes` maps a task class to a `provider/model` (or alias) or an object `{target, candidates, fallback, fallback_on, strategy}`. A `/<task> text` turn (task declared in `routes`, never `chat`) uses that route; plain turns use the selected model, plus `routes.chat` fallback and strategy when present. Candidates are tried in order, each at most once per turn. Only connect, timeout, rate-limit and server failures (and a stream cut before the first chunk) fall back; a failure after the first chunk shows `stream interrupted from <provider>` and never re-sends. `fallback_on: "any"` also falls back on auth or refused failures. `strategy` is `cheapest` (cost_per_mtok, local = 0) or `fastest` (in-memory latency EWMA). A breaker skips a provider after 3 consecutive retryable failures for a 30 s cooldown, announced once. Every failure is one `error: <provider>: <class>: <reason>` line via `harnessSource`'s `notify` option. JSON, SSE and NDJSON replies normalise to the same deltas. `/auth` in harness mode lists env key status offline (H-R24). Breaker skip (H-R16) is flashed as a one-frame hint, since the transcript repaints every frame. Ctrl-c during a streamed harness reply aborts the request, shows `cancelled`, and never falls back (H-R21). Token counts come from the provider's `usage` (or chars/4 marked `~`), and a local provider's cost is `$0` <!-- metrics-verified: chat/harness.mjs usageOf sets cost = 0 for is_local providers --> (H-R22). `/detect` probes only loopback `detect_candidates` (ports or loopback URLs) and only when asked; other hosts are listed as skipped (H-R23).
